issues.description: Check directory name does not match the CHANGELOG/metadata CheckID consistency expectations
issues.detail: The PR description refers to 'compute_instance_multiple_network_interfaces' as the new check, but the actual directory, file, class, and CheckID are 'compute_instance_single_network_interface'. While internally consistent, this mismatch with the PR title/description suggests the naming was changed late; verify intent and confirm the CheckID is the desired final name since it is user-facing in reports and hub URLs.

issues.description: GKE detection via name prefix 'gke-' is fragile and user-spoofable
issues.detail: Identifying GKE-managed nodes by checking instance.name.startswith('gke-') is unreliable: users can name any VM with that prefix to silently downgrade FAIL to MANUAL, and GKE node naming conventions are not contractually stable. Prefer detecting GKE via labels (e.g., 'goog-gke-node') or metadata, which GKE applies authoritatively.

issues.description: MANUAL status not documented in metadata or covered by framework expectations
issues.detail: The check emits status='MANUAL' for GKE instances, but the metadata.json does not describe this outcome and most Prowler checks only use PASS/FAIL/MANUAL via a known framework convention. Confirm Check_Report_GCP and the reporting/UI pipeline actually support 'MANUAL' as a status value; otherwise these findings may be silently dropped or break downstream consumers.

issues.description: Zero-interface branch leaves status as PASS, which is semantically questionable
issues.detail: When interface_count == 0, status remains 'PASS' with message 'has no network interfaces'. A VM with zero NICs is unusual and arguably not a passing state for a check titled 'has a single network interface'. Consider INFO/MANUAL, or at minimum a clearer disposition, since the current PASS may mislead operators reviewing the report.

issues.description: Default '' for network/subnetwork could collide with real values and lose information
issues.detail: In _get_instances, network and subnetwork are split on '/' and stored as the last segment, defaulting to ''. Empty string is indistinguishable from 'missing' vs 'unset'. Using Optional[str] = None would be clearer and prevent future bugs where downstream checks compare against literal ''.

issues.description: No test asserts FAIL on GKE-prefixed name with single NIC or non-GKE name like 'gke-foo-myapp'
issues.detail: Tests cover single NIC, multi NIC, mixed, and a GKE multi-NIC case, but do not assert behavior for an instance whose name happens to start with 'gke-' but has a single NIC, nor for adversarial naming. Adding a couple of edge cases would harden the GKE branch and document intent.

review.summary: The PR adds a sensible GCP compute check with good test coverage for the main scenarios. Main concerns: (1) the PR title/description name ('compute_instance_multiple_network_interfaces') doesn't match the actual CheckID ('compute_instance_single_network_interface'), which is the user-facing identifier; (2) GKE detection via name prefix is fragile and spoofable, and should use GKE-applied labels; (3) the MANUAL status path needs confirmation that downstream reporting supports it. Other items are minor (zero-NIC PASS semantics, empty-string defaults, and missing edge-case tests).
